independence_statement: All probes below were written by the HQ245 reviewer. They do not import or reuse the author's Stage A test module or any of its helpers. Author's tests were run separately only as a baseline.

reproduction_scripts.purpose: under/over length lie, tuple subclass, factory refusal
P1-P9 custody/invariant probes and leak measurements
ASAN reproduction of the OOB read

blocking_crash_reproduction.input: class EvilList(list): def __len__(self): return 5  -- constructed over a 1-element list
blocking_crash_reproduction.observed: SIGSEGV, shell exit 139, three consecutive runs 139/139/139
blocking_crash_reproduction.asan_observed: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x8 (READ); PyObject_GetAttrString+0xe <- StageAOwner_init _p07_native_owner_stage_a.c:265; rdi=0x0
blocking_crash_reproduction.verdict: native memory-safety defect reachable from ordinary Python

length_lie_characterization.list_subclass_len_under_report: no crash; n_relations admitted = 1 for a 3-element subclass (silent truncation)
length_lie_characterization.tuple_subclass_len_over_report: no segfault in this run, but the loop still indexed past the true end and raised 'relation[1] must expose ref' from garbage memory -- an out-of-bounds read either way
length_lie_characterization.module_factory_build_stage_a_owner_with_: REFUSED with TypeError ('requires an exact list/tuple of relations') because the factory uses Py_TYPE(relations) == &PyList_Type
length_lie_characterization.conclusion: the bounds bug lives in the class __init__ path, not the convenience factory; the type is public and __new__ + __init__ is normal Python

P1_registry_is_decorative.mechanism: the only check is `registry == Py_None`; registry content is never read; registry_key stores Py_TYPE(registry)->tp_name
P1_registry_is_decorative.impact: the claimed 'requires explicit registry' binding is nominal at Stage A

P2_custody_diagnostic_leak.verdict: unbounded refcount leak on a public method

P3_repeated_failing_init_leak.verdict: unbounded refcount/memory leak on the partial-failure/reinit path

P4_trusted_semantic_hash_never_invoked.observed: 0 calls during construction and two resolve_exact calls
P4_trusted_semantic_hash_never_invoked.impact: the advertised TCB seam is dead code at Stage A; it cannot re-verify any projection because it is never used

P5_identity_reverification_is_string_onl.observed: a mutable stand-in admitted with fixed ref.key and content_hash, then its semantic_payload flipped from DENIED to AUTHORIZED_AFTER_SEAL, is still returned by resolve_exact as trusted (got is s)
P5_identity_reverification_is_string_onl.impact: re-verification detects only ref.key/content_hash string changes; it does not re-derive semantic_projection, consistent with the author's own caveat, and confirms a material edge case Stage B must close

P6_unsealed_new.observed: resolve_exact on __new__-only object refused: 'stage A owner is not sealed'

P9_source_vs_empty_victim.empty_victim_resolve: refused: 'exact SourceUniverseRelation unavailable from native owner custody; no label/ID/latest/default inference'

stress.malformed_resolve_loop: 200000 randomized malformed inputs (None, int, float, str, bytes, list, dict, partial mappings, non-unicode components, callables), no crash
stress.malformed_constructor_loop: 50000 randomized malformed constructor inputs, no crash
stress.reinit_on_sealed: 1000 attempts refused, sealed stays True, custody unchanged
stress.resolve_path_memory_differential: 50000 vs 500000 resolves in fresh processes: maxrss 9961472 vs 9883648 bytes -> no leak attributable to resolve_exact
